The planned merger of two major streaming platforms, HBO Max and Paramount+, may ultimately fall through.

The plan was announced in March of this year, when Netflix withdrew from the bidding war for Warner Bros. Discovery. However, a federal judge has now issued a temporary restraining order to block the deal from going through — at least for now…

The original merger plan

The deal was originally for Paramount to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, after which the two companies' streaming platforms, HBO Max and Paramount+, would be integrated into a single service.

Temporary restraining order

Audiences have not been particularly enthusiastic about the plan, worrying it would reduce competition and drive up prices. A coalition of 12 state attorneys general shared the same concerns and petitioned a federal court to issue a temporary restraining order on the deal. According to NBC News, the request has been granted.

The temporary restraining order lasts for 14 days, during which a hearing will be held. Even if Paramount ultimately prevails, the merger will still be subject to review by the European Union and the UK government. The Writers Guild of America has also filed an antitrust lawsuit, arguing that the merger would lead to job losses and lower pay.
